candidates.designation: 13.6 d RV signal (Palle et al. 2023, Sect. 4.3.1 and Table 5); exoplanet.eu calls it TOI-4481 d
candidates.tier_reason: Single-paper RV signal the discoverers explicitly could not separate from stellar activity: seen in CARMENES and HIRES but NOT recovered in MAROON-X, which covers two cycles with enough precision to see it; a 13.6 d photometric peak also appears in LCO B-band photometry, and the rotation period is not pinned down. They did not adopt it in their final model.
candidates.orbit_flags: RV only (CARMENES + HIRES). P, K = 4.10 +/- 0.20 m/s, Msini and a from the paper's reference-model fit (Table 5); eccentricity not given (circular fit implied). Not detected in MAROON-X; the 13.6 d period may be activity-related. Possible near-2:1 with c (6.64 d). Table 5 in the arXiv PDF text is column-shifted; values read as P 13.60588(65), t0 2417.23+/-0.12, K 4.10+/-0.20, a/R* 48.8, Msini 8.50+/-0.45, a 0.0844+/-0.0017 AU, Teq 385 K, S 3.6 S_earth.

candidates.designation: kappa CrB c (Bonsor et al. 2013, Sect. 3.2); 'putative outer body' causing the RV trend (Lovell et al. 2022, Sect. 6)
candidates.tier_reason: Only a linear RV trend - no period, no orbit. The trend is now highly significant (0.73 +/- 0.07 m/s/yr over 17 yr) and persists, but its source is unconstrained: 0.4-120 MJup at 8-66 AU, so it may be a giant planet, a brown dwarf or an M dwarf. Lovell et al. add that the acceleration 'may not necessarily be due to an outer planet'. No imaging detection (Keck AO) and no Gaia-Hipparcos proper-motion anomaly.
candidates.orbit_flags: RV acceleration only: dv/dt = 1.51 +/- 0.52 m/s/yr over 8.09 yr (Bonsor+2013, Table 1); 0.73 +/- 0.07 m/s/yr (N=1 fit) and 0.83 +/- 0.27 m/s/yr (N=2 fit) over 17 yr (Lovell+2022, Table 5 - the PDF text columns are shifted, values read by row). Published constraints, not orbit fits: a = 8-66 AU, mass 0.4-120 MJup (Lovell+2022 abstract and Sect. 6); Doppler excludes planets <13 MJup beyond ~40 AU (Bonsor+2013 Sect. 3.2). The RadVel N=2 solution (c: P ~3936 d, Msini 0.39 MJup, a 6.0 AU, e 0.78) was rejected by the authors as dynamically unstable - do not use it as an orbit. No period, a, e or Msini to enter.
candidates.reference: Bonsor et al. 2013, MNRAS (doi:10.1093/mnras/stt367), 'Spatially resolved images of dust belt(s) around the planet-hosting subgiant kappa CrB', Sect. 2.1, 3.2, Table 1; Lovell et al. 2022, MNRAS 517, 2546, Sect. 6, Table 5
